XREX command flow

The serial commands for one Transrex shot, in the order the controller accepts them, and the path out of a fault. Check the reply to each command before sending the next.

The hub logs and announces this as a dangerous command Fault path <ch> is the channel, 1 to 4

When fault pins are read

Water, temperature, Enerpro and overcurrent pins are all polled continuously (water, temperature and Enerpro since firmware built 2026-11-09; older images read them only on a pin change, at boot and in FAULT:CLEar). A disabled channel's pins are ignored. FAULT:CLEar in IDLE or ARMED does nothing. In FAULT, STATE? ends with ACTIVE=, the list of every fault measured.

Commands that act outside IDLE

SOURce:ENAble, XREX:CHANnel:ENAOut and CONTactOut take effect immediately in any state. While ARMED or FIRING, an enabled channel whose ready lines are not both HIGH faults, so set the lines before enabling.

A reset forgets the setup

A !BOOT line can arrive at any time. Enables, gains and shot timing are gone: nothing is recalled at boot. Re-identify, tell the operator, and set up again or recall a saved profile (*RCL <slot>, eight slots, IDLE only; CONFig:PROFile:DIFF? <slot> shows first what it would change). Do not resend the old setup silently.

Saved profiles and the dead time

A profile keeps the control rates and calibration, the fault polarities, the shot timing and, per channel, the gains, loop mode and currents. It does not keep channel enables, the ready lines or the external-enable setting. CONFig:DEADtime <ns> (50 to 3000, 100 at every boot) is announced as dangerous and is not in a profile on XREX.

Events

The live !EVT lines are off at every boot since 2026-11-09 (SYS:EVENT 1 turns them on for this boot). A program that polls STATE? needs nothing else; SYS:EVLOG? has the history either way.

Not on this chart

DEBUG:FAULT:BYPASS 1 makes the controller ignore its fault detection. It is for a bench with nothing connected and is not a recovery step.

Sources: docs/labview_commands.md, docs/labview_state_and_faults.md, firmware/xrex/docs/command_reference.md, and the XREX firmware in WHAM-CONTROLLERS. Amps are a placeholder calibration until measured on a real Transrex.
